**Analysis:**

This is a microscopic image (100 µm scale bar, credit: Bruce Watt) showing fungal/oomycete reproductive structures. Key features:

- **Lemon/oval-shaped sporangia** (~40-60 µm), ellipsoidal with granular contents
- **Long, thin, curved sporangiophores** bearing the sporangia
- **Papilla** visible at the apical attachment point of the central sporangiophore cluster
- Sympodially-branched sporangiophore arrangement

These are classic *Phytophthora infestans* sporangia — the diagnostic microscopic structures of **Late Blight**. The lemon-shaped sporangia with a papilla borne on sporangiophores are textbook *P. infestans* morphology, matching the symptom description which specifically notes "white fuzzy pathogen sporulation" on leaves/stems. The sporangia size (~40-60 µm at this scale) is consistent with *P. infestans*.

No other class in the list produces this structure: Rhizopus has columellate sporangia on erect sporangiophores; Gray Mold (*Botrytis*) has grape-like conidial clusters; Leaf Mold (*Fulvia fulva*) has olive-colored conidia chains.
